newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Feb 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After creating a storm last year with his A$2.87 million salary for the 1994-95 financial year, former Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels has received 200,000 free Coles Myer shares worth A$1 million as part of his exit package. Coles had not publicised the terms of Bartels departure, but the information was contained in the company's 20F filing with the US Securities and Exchange last week. Page 19.

The town of Guadalcanal is the site of political and corporate infighting which may have a dramatic effect on the future of Australian gold house Ross Mining, as the people of Guadalcanal were to hold a rally to consider blockading Ross Mining's A$69 million Gold Ridge project. Page 19.

A two-year plan devised in conjunction with McKinsey & Co will see building materials giant CSR slash costs in it A$1 billion timber division by A$140 million and target aggressive cost savings in its local building and construction materials operations. age 19.

After announcing yet another loss on Friday, base metals giant MIM Holdings Ltd has announced it has been forced to cut its dividend but MIM managing director Nick Stumps has told shareholders there are encouraging signs for base metals prices without proising a return to the black. Page 20.

North Ltd managing director Campbell Andersen said yesterday the company would quickly expand on its $300 million move into the North American iron ore industry after foreshadowing further investment in Canada's largest iron ore producer, Iron Ore Companyof Canada. Page 20.

Savage Resources Ltd managing director Jim Wall has announced the diversified mining company will proceed with the long-awaited A$340 million expansion of its Clarkesville refinery in the US as part of a three-pronged strategy to increase its exposure to inc. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian States are still bickering over draft proposals for national access to gas pipelines and the dismantling of barriers to interstate trade, three years after the Council of Australian Governments approved the proposal. The bickering threatens fudamental reforms in Australia's gas industry could cause the collapse of the entire proposal. Page 17.

Negotiations between Aboriginal land owners and Pasminco Ltd's on the future of the Century Zinc project in the Queensland Gulf are expected to reach an historic accord despite a chance they may breech a February 13 deadline. The two groups appear close to an agreement on the development of the mine after crucial talks during the past three weeks. Page 17.

Business leaders attending the annual World Economic Forum in Switzerland have been warned that financial turbulence in three critical economic zones - Europe, Japan and the US - threatens the benign outlook for the world economy. A hint of the turbulence has undermined the Australian dollar recently, sending it to an 18-month low. Page 17.

Steaming coal producers have been forced to accept price cuts in negotiations with Japanese power utilities, although AME Mineral Economics coal analyst Clyde Henderson said the cuts could have been worse for the industry if the exchange rate had stayed around its high level of US82c in early December. Page 17.

Equatorial mining has urged shareholders not to accept a A30c a share takeover offer from the AMP society. The AMP bid was increased from 25c on Friday, valuing Equatorial at A95 million, but an independent report by Grant Samuel and Associates has valued the company at between A36c and 47c a share. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Reserve Bank will hold its monthly policy-making board meeting tomorrow, and it seems certain home-loan and business interest rates will not see a cut. Financial market analysts believe the release of wage data this week and the unresolved ACTU's livig wage will see the central bank reserve its decision on rate cuts. Page 35.

Faced with structural change in the Australian building products market, and a sharemarket growing impatient, CSR chief executive Geoff Kells is taking the knife to the group in the form of a plan to raise more than A$1 billion from asset sales. Page 35.

The latest National Australian Bank business expectations survey has revealed an increase in business expectations for output and profitability and a bleak outlook for unemployment, prompting the bank to change its pro-interest rate cut stance. Page 35.

Mining giant Placer Dome is expecting to take a 90 per cent stake in Highlands Gold by this Friday after increasing its holding in the company to 76.5 per cent. Placer Dome paid A$316.1 million for Highland's 25 per cent stake in the Porgera goldmine, with its 75c-a-share offer closing this Saturday. Page 37.

In what could be the beginning of a shake-up of St Barbara Mines ownership, founding shareholder of St Barbara mines, Ross Atkins, has sold his 7.7 per cent stake in the company. The shares were bought by Westgold Resources for 80c each late last week. Page 38.

The AMP societies new chief financial officer Paul Batchelor looks set to take the company through demutualisation and public listing. Batchelor orchestrated the Colonial Group's takeover of the State Bank of New South Wales and its demutualisation. AMP wll be one of Australia's largest companies when publicly listed. Page 37
THE AGE

Telstra Corp is facing a $400 million shortfall in it crucial pre-float year apparently due to competition for international and STD calls. Austel chairman Neil Tuckwell confirmed Telstra rivals were making inroads into the international market and said Telstra's share had fallen below 60 per cent for the first time. Page C1.

US Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers claims the United States economic expansion is the best balanced since the 1960s and has a long way to run. US growth was being led by investment and underpinned by low inflation, indicating the prospect of ovrheating and tighter monetary policy was quite remote, Summers told a press conference at the annual World Economic Forum. Page C1.

National Australia Bank's business survey for the December quarter predicts the economy will be running at a four per cent growth rate by the second half of this year. The survey found slightly improved conditions in some sectors with a great deal of varince. The NAB forecasts 2.75 per cent growth this financial year, with unemployment still around eight per cent in June 1998. Page C3.

Unions and members face A$2000 fines for refusing to lift industrial action as the Federal Court is about to hear a landmark industrial dispute. Mobil Australia applied to the court to force three unions to abide by an order banning industrial action. The Australian Council of Trade Unions criticised the legal sanctions as a mass meeting of unions will be held on Wednesday to discuss legal action and industrial strategy. Page C3.

Low inflation figures look set to provide room for another home loan interest rate cut. Rates have dropped 1.5 percentage points since July last year as the four leading banks offer a standard variable rate of 8.25 per cent to all customers. Non-bank lenders are struggling to undercut the banks basic loans, and may soon offer branded credit card and insurance products to customers. Page C5.

Mount Edon Gold mines posted a A$5 million first half profit after its share price plunged in 1996. The profit is a A$10 million turn around for Mount Edon, which is fighting off a takeover by Camelot Resources. Mount Edon managing director Mr Tony Brenna says the takeover is opportunistic in the light of the profit. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
